title: One rule for unplaceable references, and a guess never blocks
summary: This change adds `unplaceable-reference`, a single writing rule that replaces six older reference rules (bare-reference, reference-without-label, reference-without-link, chat-local-reference, undefined-name, undefined-name-at-start). It scans each paragraph for four kinds of candidate — a number, a phrase, a time, a name — and reports the ones the paragraph itself does not place. Alongside it, `osf-lint-core::resolve` gains an `Evidence` argument: a finding backed only by statistical evidence always resolves to a warning with advice, in every context, class and group, so a guess can never refuse a reply. The rule is wired into the writing lint, the skill lint and the scan resolver, and is measured by a 96-fixture precision/recall harness plus end-to-end stop-hook and commit-message tests.

lanes.label: Entry points
lanes.subtitle: hooks, CLI, commit check
lanes.summary: The surfaces that hand text to the linter: the stop hook, the prompt hook, the commit-message check and the scan command.

lanes.label: Lint core
lanes.subtitle: osf-lint-core
lanes.summary: Shared rule machinery: the class/group/context/evidence resolver and the segmenter that splits text into paragraphs and sentences.

lanes.label: Writing lints
lanes.subtitle: crates/osf/src/lints
lanes.summary: The writing rule set, including the new reference candidate finder and its placement checks.

lanes.label: Fixtures and tests
lanes.subtitle: tests/fixtures/writing/unplaceable
lanes.summary: The 96 labelled fixtures and the harnesses that measure precision and recall and prove the rule end to end.

nodes.label: Stop hook
nodes.subtitle: hook stop
nodes.summary: Reads the last assistant message from stdin and decides whether to refuse the reply. A refusal now requires a deterministic finding; a weak-evidence name alone no longer refuses.

nodes.label: Prompt hook
nodes.subtitle: hook prompt
nodes.summary: Prints the reminder text on every prompt. It must never name a retired rule id, which the new end-to-end test checks.

nodes.label: Commit-message check
nodes.subtitle: osf lint writing --context commit
nodes.summary: Lints a commit message file. The same relative time that a transcript may use fails here, because commit context is durable text.

nodes.label: Scan resolver
nodes.subtitle: scan::resolve_and_explain
nodes.summary: Resolves level and remediation for scan findings, now passing each finding's own evidence into the shared resolver.

nodes.label: resolve()
nodes.subtitle: class, group, context, exception, evidence
nodes.summary: The one place a finding's level and remediation are decided. A new first branch returns warning plus advise for statistical evidence, before any class, group, context or exception is consulted.

nodes.label: Segmenter
nodes.subtitle: segment::parse
nodes.summary: Splits text into paragraphs and sentences and reduces inline markup. The new rule re-parses each paragraph to get sentence spans and reduced text.

nodes.label: lint_writing()
nodes.subtitle: crates/osf/src/lints/writing/mod.rs
nodes.summary: Runs the writing rules in order and applies context. It now calls unplaceable_reference after undefined_names, and passes evidence through to rule resolution for the new rule only.

nodes.label: unplaceable_reference()
nodes.subtitle: rules.rs
nodes.summary: Collects candidates per paragraph, picks one paragraph to report each repeated name from, and emits a finding for every candidate the paragraph does not place.

nodes.label: candidates()
nodes.subtitle: reference.rs
nodes.summary: Finds number, phrase, time and name candidates in one paragraph, masking quoted and backticked spans first and keeping only the longest candidate of each kind when two overlap.

nodes.label: Placement checks
nodes.subtitle: is_placed and friends
nodes.summary: Decides whether a candidate is placed: a link, a bracketed or colon description, a repository or file name in the same clause, an absolute date, a known name, a definer sentence or a mention marker.

nodes.label: Rule metadata
nodes.subtitle: writing/meta.rs
nodes.summary: Holds each rule's class, group, exception and doc text. It gains the unplaceable-reference entry and a resolve() that now takes evidence.

nodes.label: Known names
nodes.subtitle: writing/names.rs
nodes.summary: The built-in name list, extended with frameworks, design systems and model tiers, plus a new is_generic_word helper so a generic label word never counts as a name.

nodes.label: Unplaceable fixtures
nodes.subtitle: 96 labelled markdown files
nodes.summary: Each fixture carries an osf-unplaceable header naming its label, kind, target and reason, and an osf-expect block naming the rules that must fire.

nodes.label: Precision/recall harness
nodes.subtitle: unplaceable_measure.rs
nodes.summary: Runs the rule over every fixture, matches findings to targets by containment, and requires 100% precision and recall with no stray findings, excluding the model kind.

nodes.label: Checkpoint tests
nodes.subtitle: unplaceable_checkpoints.rs
nodes.summary: Drives the compiled binary through the stop hook, the commit-message check and the prompt hook to prove the rule runs in the real pipeline.

edges.label: last assistant message
edges.summary: The stop hook lints the reply and refuses only on a deterministic finding; a weak-evidence name now passes.

edges.label: commit message, context commit
edges.summary: The commit-message check runs the same rule in commit context, where a relative time is a finding.

edges.label: doc, known names, context
edges.summary: The new rule is called once per document, after the older name rules, and its findings join the same list.

edges.label: one paragraph at a time
edges.summary: Each paragraph is scanned for candidates before any placement decision is made.

edges.label: is_placed
edges.summary: Every candidate is tested against the paragraph, its following list items and its sentences.

edges.label: parse paragraph text
edges.summary: The candidate finder re-parses the paragraph to get sentence spans and reduced sentence text.

edges.label: known name lookup
edges.summary: A word followed by a number is excluded when the word is a known name and not a generic label word.

edges.label: resolve(context, evidence)
edges.summary: Context application now passes the finding's evidence for the new rule, and deterministic evidence for the older rules until they are retired.

edges.label: class, group, context, exception, evidence
edges.summary: Rule metadata forwards its class, group and exception plus the caller's evidence into the shared resolver.

edges.label: finding evidence
edges.summary: Scan findings now carry their own evidence into resolution, so a statistical scan finding also only advises.

edges.label: lint_writing per fixture
edges.summary: The harness calls the rule directly over every fixture and asserts perfect precision and recall.

edges.label: osf hook stop with stdin
edges.summary: The end-to-end tests spawn the real binary and feed it a stop event.

edges.label: label, kind, target, reason
edges.summary: Each fixture's header is parsed into a labelled case the harness scores.

flows.title: A reply is linted at the stop hook
flows.summary: The stop hook reads the last assistant message, lints it in transcript context, and refuses only when a deterministic finding survives. A weak-evidence name is reported as advice and never refuses.

messages.label: refuse only on a deterministic error
messages.note: A statistical finding resolves to warning plus advise, so it never reaches the refusal path.

views.title: Writing lint architecture
views.summary: The entry points that lint text, the shared resolver, the writing rule set with the new reference rule, and the fixture corpus that measures it.

views.title: Inside the reference rule
views.summary: How one paragraph becomes candidates and then findings: candidate finding, placement checks, and the evidence that decides the level.

children.title: Evidence decides the level
children.summary: The new first branch in resolve: statistical evidence returns warning plus advise before class, group, context or exception is read.
